title: AssetCore UAT
headline: Work through it, mark what breaks
tagline: Round 3: the surface two rounds never reached — QR labels, the scan page, stock movement, report files, and the cross-cutting checks nobody has run. Six failures found, six fixed and re-run.
intro: Rounds 1 and 2 closed 14 defects but left 17 of round 1's original untested cases still untested, and re-clicked only some of round 1's JavaScript-driven passes. This round goes after exactly that: the parts of the app that have never been watched working. It also re-checks the round-2 fixes that a later change could plausibly have broken. Run against a local stack — API on 8787, app on 5174, database assetcore_integrate — not staging. The run found six failures and recorded them before anything was changed; each was then fixed and the same card re-run in the browser. Every note below keeps the original finding and says what changed underneath it. One card is still not run: keyboard activation, which this session's synthetic keys cannot prove either way.
url_hint: The app runs at http://localhost:5174 and the API at http://localhost:8787. Ask Claude Code to start them both if the link is dead.

sections.title: Labels, scanning and the field loop
sections.blurb: The technician's path: print a label, scan it, find the asset. Round 1 listed this as r1t48 and never ran it.

tests.title: Print a sheet of QR labels from the asset list
tests.intro: The codebase carries components/AssetQr.jsx — a QR code and a printable label sheet with its own print stylesheet. This test asks whether a user can reach it.
steps: Assets → select two or three assets.
Look for a Labels, QR or Print action on the list or in the row menu.
Open it and check the sheet previews one label per asset.
tests.expect: A label sheet opens showing one QR per selected asset with its AIN beneath, and Print produces the same sheet.
tests.notes:
No such control exists. As the owner on Assets I looked at every control on the page and in each row: STATE and HEALTH filter chips, Archived, Import CSV, Add Asset, a search box, type and location selects, and per-row View / Edit / WO. There is no row selection, no Labels, no QR, no Print — read_page's interactive list confirms it, and searching the page for 'label', 'QR' and 'print' returns nothing. The asset detail panel has no QR either (its actions are Complete Maintenance, Raise Work Order, Edit Asset, Archive). Cause: apps/app/src/components/AssetQr.jsx exports assetQrValue(), AssetQrCode and PrintQrSheet — a working QR label and a printable 4-up sheet with its own print stylesheet — and nothing in the app imports any of them. Grepping the whole client for 'AssetQr' matches only the file's own export line. The feature is written and unreachable. (apps/app/src/components/DocumentsPanel.jsx is dead in the same way.)

FIXED AND RE-RUN. AssetQr.jsx is now imported by the asset register: a Labels button sits between Import CSV and Add Asset, and it prints whatever the filters have narrowed the list to — so 'labels for the Warri site' is a search away rather than a feature. Watched it: searched 'Warri' (2 rows), pressed Labels, and the sheet opened as 'Print asset labels — 2 labels · 4 per row' with two rendered QR SVGs captioned NGML-VLV-0089 / Warri T-A Isolation Valve 089 and NGML-SCR-041 / Warri Terminal A RTU — exactly the filtered list, nothing else. The codes encode ${origin}/scan?ain=<AIN>, the path card 04 proved resolves. Pressing Print could not be completed here: the pane blocks pop-ups, so window.open returned null and the component's own fallback fired — 'Your browser blocked the print window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.' (caught in the console as a suppressed alert). The preview IS the print source, so what was watched is what would come out; the print dialog itself needs a browser that allows pop-ups. DocumentsPanel.jsx is still dead — wiring it is a feature decision, not this repair.

tests.title: Scan page: look up a real tag by hand
tests.intro: The scan page takes a camera feed or a typed tag. The camera cannot be driven here; the manual path can, and it is the same lookup.
steps: Open /scan.
Type NGML-MTR-0042 into the manual field and submit.
Read the asset card that comes back.
tests.expect: The Lagos DS-04 Metering Station card appears with its status, criticality and commissioned date — the date filled in, not blank (round 2 fixed the column name behind it).
tests.notes:
As the Field Technician on /scan, typed NGML-MTR-0042 and pressed Find: the card returned 'Lagos DS-04 Metering Station' with badges operational / medium criticality / Lagos DS-04, Category 'Metering Station', and — the point of the retest — Installed reading 2020-09-07 rather than blank, so round 2's commission_date→install_date fix holds on this screen. FOUND WHILE HERE, not part of the pass condition: three of the six fields on this card can never be filled. It reads asset.manufacturer, asset.serial_number and asset.warranty_expiry (Scan.jsx:197-200), but the asset edit form and the CSV importer both write manufacturer/model/serial into the specs JSONB (assets.ts:355-358), and every row in the table has NULL in the real columns. I set NGML-MTR-0042's manufacturer to 'UAT R3 Instruments' earlier in this round: the asset list shows it, the scan card still shows '—'. Custodian is blank for the same class of reason.

FIXED SINCE: the scan card now reads manufacturer/model/serial through the column first and the specs JSONB second (Scan.jsx), so the values the asset form actually writes are visible. Re-run as the Field Technician on /scan?ain=NGML-MTR-0042: Manufacturer now reads 'UAT R3 Instruments' — the value set earlier in this round that the card used to swallow. Serial and Warranty stay '—' because this asset genuinely has neither. The underlying split — two homes for the same field, columns that nothing populates — is left as it is and is worth a migration decision rather than a UAT patch.

tests.title: Scan page: an unknown tag is refused in a sentence
tests.intro: A label from another site, or a smudged read. The page must say so rather than showing a code or an empty card.
steps: On /scan, enter NGML-NOPE-9999.
Read the message.
tests.expect: A sentence naming the tag — no raw not_found, no blank card.
tests.notes: Entered NGML-NOPE-9999. The card cleared and the page showed: 'No asset with tag “NGML-NOPE-9999” in this organisation.' — a sentence naming the tag, no raw not_found, no empty card left on screen.

tests.title: A scan URL opens the asset directly
tests.intro: A printed label encodes /scan?ain=… so a phone camera opens the asset. That query parameter path has never been exercised.
steps: Navigate to http://localhost:5174/scan?ain=NGML-VLV-0089 directly.
Check the asset resolves without typing anything.
tests.expect: The Warri T-A Isolation Valve card renders from the URL alone.
tests.notes: Navigated straight to http://localhost:5174/scan?ain=NGML-VLV-0089 with no typing. The page loaded with the field pre-filled 'NGML-VLV-0089' and the card already resolved to 'Warri T-A Isolation Valve 089' (operational, medium criticality, Warri Terminal A). This is the path a printed label would use — it works, even though nothing in the app can print that label (see card 01).

sections.title: Stock actually moves
sections.blurb: Round 2 proved a part could be reserved on a job. Nobody has yet watched stock fall when the job closes — r1t37's other half.

tests.title: Closing a work order draws its reserved parts out of stock
tests.intro: consumeParts() in workOrders.ts runs on the transition to closed: it decrements quantity_in_stock, writes a stock movement and stamps consumed_at. Round 2 left WO-2025-0041 holding one reserved SP-PT-1100 against a stock of 2.
steps: Note the on-hand figure for SP-PT-1100 on Spare Parts.
Open WO-2025-0041 and close it.
Return to Spare Parts and read the on-hand figure again.
Open the part and look for the issue in its movement history.
tests.expect: On-hand falls from 2 to 1, the work order's part line reads as consumed rather than reserved, and a movement row records the issue against the job.
tests.notes: Watched end to end. Before: Spare Parts showed SP-PT-1100 at '2 each' with a Reorder badge and a stock value of ₦370,000; WO-2025-0041 carried '1× · SP-PT-1100 · 2 in stock · Reserved · ₦185,000'. Pressed Closed on the job: toast 'Work order moved to Closed.', activity logged 'Status changed to Closed · Adaeze Okeke · 8 Sept, 15:51'. After: the job's part line reads '1× · SP-PT-1100 · 1 in stock · Taken', Spare Parts reads '1 each' and stock value ₦185,000, and the part's movement history opens with '-1 · Used on job · → 1 · WO-2025-0041 · Consumed on work order · Adaeze Okeke' above the earlier '-6 Issue → 2' and '+8 Receipt → 8'. The ledger reconciles to the balance on every row.

tests.title: A job cannot be closed against stock that isn't there
tests.intro: insufficient_stock (409) with a shortfall list is one of the app's own stated rules. Reserving more than exists and closing is the only way to reach it.
steps: On an open work order, reserve SP-PT-1100 with a quantity above what is on hand (say 50).
Try to close the job.
tests.expect: The close is refused in a readable sentence naming the shortfall — not a raw insufficient_stock, and the stock figure does not go negative.
tests.notes:
Reserved 50× SP-PT-1100 on WO-2025-0042 against 1 on hand — the panel showed '50× · 1 in stock · Reserved · ₦9.3M' — then pressed Closed. Refused with a red toast reading 'There is not enough on hand for that issue.' The job stayed Assigned, the line stayed Reserved, and the store still read 1 each: nothing was half-consumed and stock did not go negative. GAP, and the reason this is a qualified pass: the API answers 409 with a shortfalls array naming each part and the amount missing, and the UI throws that away — the sentence names neither the part nor the shortfall. With one line that is obvious; with five it is not. The 50× line was deleted afterwards, so the job is back as it was.

GAP CLOSED: the shortfall detail is now carried out of the API response onto the error (apiClient.js) and spelled out on screen. Re-run with 12× reserved against 1 on hand: 'Not enough stock to close this job: SP-PT-1100 — need 12, 1 on hand.' The job stayed Assigned and stock stayed at 1. The test line was deleted afterwards.

sections.title: Reports produce a file
sections.blurb: r1t43: generate a report and check the file against what the screen says. Never run, and the generator was rewritten from a stub.

tests.title: Request and generate a report, then compare it to the screen
tests.intro: POST /reports/:id/generate builds a real XLSX or CSV synchronously and records a byte size. The check that matters is whether the file's row count agrees with the list it claims to report.
steps: Reports → request an asset register as CSV.
Generate it and wait for Ready.
Note the row count implied by the Assets page (6 assets).
Download the file and open it.
tests.expect: Status goes pending → ready with a non-zero size, and the file holds a header row plus one row per asset, matching the Assets list.
tests.notes:
Reports → Generate Report → Asset Register, output CSV, Generate. The row appeared as 'Asset Register — 8 Sept 2026', CSV, 1 KB, Ready, with a Download action; pressing Download issued GET /api/files/reports/ca722304…csv → 200 (the pane's sandbox blocks the save itself, so the file was read from where the API wrote it, apps/api/data/files/<org>/reports/). The file holds a header row plus exactly six data rows, one per asset, and the figures agree with the screen: health 69 / 61 / 74 / 88 / 18 / 92 against the same six values in the Asset Registry, and NGML-MTR-0042's book value 148,800,000 against the ₦148,800,000.00 on its asset panel. SMALL DEFECT: immediately after generating, the BY column reads '—'. POST /reports and /reports/:id/generate both return the raw row, which has no created_by_profile — only the list query joins the user. Reloading the page fills it in with 'Adaeze Okeke'. Cosmetic and momentary, but it is the one figure on that row nobody can check by eye.

SMALL DEFECT FIXED: POST /reports and /reports/:id/generate now re-select through the same query the list uses, so the row they return carries created_by_profile. Re-run: generated a Work Order Summary as the owner and the BY column read 'Adaeze Okeke' immediately, with no reload. Two assertions in uatRound3.test.ts hold it.

tests.title: A report the Viewer must not be able to request
tests.intro: Round 2 gated GET /reports on report:read and left the Viewer holding it through *:read. report:create is a different capability — the Viewer should be able to read the page and not to generate.
steps: As the Viewer open /reports.
Look for a request/generate control, and try it if it is offered.
tests.expect: Either no create control is offered, or using it is refused in a sentence. A Viewer must not be able to write a report file.
tests.notes:
The server holds; the screen does not. As uat.viewer the Reports page renders with a '+ Generate Report' button in the header AND a Generate Report tab — both offered to a role with only *:read. Picking Asset Register and pressing Generate Report sends POST /api/reports, which is correctly refused 403 Forbidden — and the user is told nothing at all. No toast, no inline message, no change of state; the button just sits there. Cause: handleGenerate catches the error into setErr (Reports.jsx:83) but `err` is only rendered inside the Report Library branch (Reports.jsx:128), and setTab('library') is only reached on success — so the message is stored on a tab the user is not on and never sees. The expectation allowed either outcome (no control, or a refusal in a sentence); neither happened. This is the F5 shape round 2 fixed elsewhere: a control offered to a role that cannot use it, with a silent refusal behind it.

FIXED AND RE-RUN. Two changes: the create affordances are gated on report:create (the header button, the Generate Report tab and the empty-state button), and the refusal message is now rendered on the generate tab as well as in the library, so a future error there cannot be silent. Re-ran as uat.viewer: /reports opens with 'Report Library' and 'Analytics' only, no Generate Report button anywhere on the page, and the Viewer can still read and download the two existing reports — which is what *:read should give them. Re-checked as the owner in the same sitting: all three tabs and both buttons still present, and a Work Order Summary generated end to end. The server-side 403 was always right and is unchanged; a test in uatRound3.test.ts holds it. HONESTY NOTE: the second change — the error rendering on the generate tab — is now unreachable for a Viewer by design, so it was verified by reading the diff rather than by watching a refusal appear.

sections.title: Round 1's JavaScript-driven passes, re-clicked
sections.blurb: These were marked passed in round 1 on evidence obtained by dispatching clicks in script rather than through the browser's input pipeline. A JS click bypasses hit-testing, so it cannot see an overlay, a disabled state or a z-index trap.

tests.title: Approval matrix: edit a band with real pointer input
tests.intro: Admin → Approvals. The band editor sets the money thresholds that route a request. Round 1 drove it in script.
steps: Admin → Approvals, open a rule and its bands.
Change a band's upper threshold and save.
Reopen it and confirm the new figure stuck.
tests.expect: The band saves and reads back with the new threshold.
tests.notes: Approvals → Matrix, real pointer clicks throughout. Opened 'UAT band — job spend ₦1,000 to ₦50,000' (floor 1000, ceiling 50000), changed the ceiling to 75000 and pressed Save rule: the matrix row redrew as '₦1,000 — ₦75,000', and reopening the editor read back 1000 / 75000 from the server rather than from local state. Restored to 50000 afterwards and confirmed the row reads '₦1,000 — ₦50,000' again, so the instance is as it was.

tests.title: Approval matrix: an impossible band is refused
tests.intro: approvals.ts:98 answers 422 invalid_band when the thresholds do not make a valid range. This is the app stating its own rule.
steps: Edit a band so its lower bound sits above its upper bound.
Save.
tests.expect: Refused with a sentence explaining the range is wrong. No raw invalid_band on screen.
tests.notes:
It is refused, but as a crash rather than as the rule. Set floor 90000 / ceiling 5000 on the existing rule and pressed Save: PATCH /api/approval-rules/028cf6d5… returned 500 Internal Server Error and the modal printed 'Something went wrong at our end. Try again, and tell an administrator if it keeps happening.' — which tells the user to escalate a mistake they could fix in two seconds. Cause: POST /approval-rules validates the band and answers 422 invalid_band (approvals.ts:97-99), and round 1 saw its sentence, 'The ceiling has to be above the floor.' The PATCH handler has no such check (approvals.ts:120-137); the DB check constraint approval_rules_check (max_amount_cents IS NULL OR max > min) raises instead, and the error escapes untyped as a 500. The create path and the edit path disagree about the same rule.

FIXED AND RE-RUN. The PATCH handler now validates the band it will produce — merging the patch over the stored row, so raising only the floor above an existing ceiling is caught too — and answers the same 422 invalid_band the create path does (approvals.ts). Re-ran the identical edit: setting the ceiling to ₦500 under a ₦1,000 floor returned 422 (was 500) and the modal now reads 'The ceiling has to be above the floor.' — word for word what round 1 saw on create — with the values still in the form to correct. Then set the ceiling back to ₦50,000 and saved: 200, and the matrix reads '₦1,000 — ₦50,000' again. Five cases pinned in apps/api/test/uatRound3.test.ts, including the floor-only patch, clearing the ceiling to null, and a rename not re-running the check.

tests.title: Nobody approves their own request
tests.intro: self_approval is the one rule an approval matrix exists to enforce. Round 2 left a pending ₦25,000 wo_cost approval routed to the Operations Manager.
steps: Raise a spend approval as the Operations Manager on any work order.
Open Approvals and try to approve that same request.
tests.expect: Refused — the approve control is absent or the attempt returns a sentence saying a requester cannot approve their own request.
tests.notes: As uat.ops — both the requester and the role the band names — set WO-2025-0042's estimated cost to ₦25,000 and pressed Request spend approval → Send for approval. The job's panel then read 'With Operations Manager · ₦25,000 · Pending'. On Approvals the counters read 'Waiting on me 1 / Mine, still pending 1 / Pending across the org 2', and the one row under Waiting on me is the OTHER request — WO-2025-0041, raised by Adaeze Okeke — with a Review action. The request I raised myself appears only under 'I submitted', and the only control on it is Recall. There is no Approve control anywhere for it, on any tab. Also worth recording: the request dialog warns before you send it — 'This job has no cost on it yet, so it will be sent as ₦0 and will only match a band that starts at zero.'

tests.title: Compliance findings: raise one on the completed audit
tests.intro: The findings flow was passed in round 1 on script-driven evidence and has one finding in the database to show for it.
steps: Compliance → open UAT R1 — ISO 14001 internal audit, Lagos DS-04.
Add a finding with a severity and a due date.
Check it appears in the audit's finding list and in any open-findings count.
tests.expect: The finding saves, shows its severity, and the audit's finding count moves with it.
tests.notes: As uat.hse, Compliance → Audits & Attestations → Findings on 'UAT R1 — ISO 14001 internal audit, Lagos DS-04'. Added a finding with clause 'ISO 14001 §9.1', text 'UAT R3 - flare stack emissions monitoring log not signed off for August.', severity Critical, due 15 Oct 2026. It saved and listed above the round-1 finding with a red 'critical' chip, the clause, and 'Due 15 Oct 26', offering Close and 'Raise a defect'. The audit row's FINDINGS column moved from '1 open of 1' to '2 open of 2', so the count follows the record. All of it with real pointer input, which is what this card was re-run for.

tests.title: Risk register: raise a risk and watch the score
tests.intro: The register scores likelihood × impact into a band. Round 1's pass never watched the band change.
steps: Risks → new risk.
Set likelihood and impact to give a high score, save.
Edit it down to a low likelihood and check the band moves.
tests.expect: The computed score and its band both change with the inputs, on the card and in the list.
tests.notes:
As uat.hse. Created 'UAT R3 — inlet flange gas release during changeover' at likelihood 4 (Has happened here before) × consequence 5 (Fatality, or loss of the facility). Saved as RSK-2026-0002: the matrix drew a red '1' in the score-20 cell, the Extreme tile went 0 → 1, Live risks 1 → 2, and the detail panel read 'BEFORE CONTROLS 20 Extreme / AFTER CONTROLS — not rated', with the honest note that the grid reads the inherent figure while no residual exists. Edited likelihood down to 1: the panel became '5 Low', Rating 1 × 5, the register row moved to 'Low 5' in both Inherent and Current, and the Extreme tile went back to 0. Score and band both follow the inputs, on the card, the register and the matrix. DEFECT FOUND HERE: on the Assess a risk form the Asset, Site and Owner pickers all read '— None —' and nothing else for this role. GET /api/assets and GET /api/sites both returned 200; GET /api/org/members returned 403 (an HSE officer has no user:manage). All three load in one Promise.all whose catch is empty — 'the register works without the pickers' (Risks.jsx:375-378) — so one forbidden call silently empties all three. Any role without user:manage therefore cannot attach a risk to an asset at all: the same shape as F6, which round 2 fixed for inspections.

DEFECT FIXED: the three pickers now load independently (Promise.allSettled in Risks.jsx) instead of all failing together when one request is refused. Re-run as uat.hse on Assess a risk: the Asset select lists all six assets and the Site select all five sites. The Owner select still shows only '— Unassigned —', which is correct — that one genuinely needs /api/org/members, and an HSE officer has no user:manage.

sections.title: Input, sessions and the edges
sections.blurb: Round 1's r1t57-64, none of which has ever been run. These are the checks that catch what feature testing cannot.

tests.title: Dark mode across the main screens
tests.intro: The app carries a dark toggle threaded through every page. Nobody has looked at it.
steps: Turn dark mode on from the topbar.
Walk Dashboard, Assets, an asset detail, Work Orders and Admin.
Look for unreadable text, white panels and charts that kept a light background.
tests.expect: Every screen is legible in dark mode: no black-on-black, no white card islands, badges and charts still readable.
tests.notes:
The theme itself is well built: turned on from the account menu, Dashboard, Assets, an asset detail, Analytics, Risk and Admin all redraw dark — sidebar, cards, the health donut, the backlog bar, the line chart and the status doughnut all adapt, and a scan for light-filled boxes wider than 80px found none. Two things fail. (1) CONTRAST. Measuring every text node against its computed background (colours are oklch, so they were resolved through a canvas): on the dashboard 18 of 143 text elements fall below WCAG AA, the worst at 1.59:1 — the empty-state line 'Preventive maintenance tasks due soon will appear here' — and the work-order reference links in Recent Work Orders at 1.79:1, which are visibly a dim blue on the dark card. Analytics is the same story (7 of 146 below AA, asset references at 1.79:1). The light theme measures 18 of 143 too, so most of this is not dark-specific — but the reference links are: they are legible in light and not in dark. (2) THE SETTING DOES NOT PERSIST. Turn dark on, reload the page, and it is light again: body background goes oklch(0.19) → oklch(0.968), there is no theme key in localStorage, and App.jsx:68 is `useState(false)` with no read of storage and no prefers-color-scheme default. A user who wants dark mode has to set it again on every page load.

FIXED AND RE-MEASURED. Three changes. (1) The theme persists: App.jsx now seeds from localStorage, falls back to prefers-color-scheme on a first visit, and writes the choice on toggle. Watched it — turned dark on, hard-reloaded, and the page came back dark with assetcore:theme='dark' stored and data-theme='dark' on <html>. (2) The brand ramp is now inverted for dark like the neutral ramp already was: --b50..--b300 become dark grounds and --b600..--b900 become light text, which is what the 1.79:1 reference links were failing on. --b400 and --b500 deliberately keep their light values (focus ring, primary button ground) so white text stays legible on them, and a new --b-solid carries the avatar fills that must always take white text in both themes. (3) --n300 is a divider step and was being used for words in five places; those moved to --n400, and dark's --n400/--n500/--n600 were lifted. Re-measured with the same script: dashboard 0 of 133 below AA, floor 5.19:1 (was 18 of 143, floor 1.59); Analytics 0 of 131, floor 4.68. No light-filled panels. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, and it should be read as outstanding: in LIGHT mode 17 of 133 elements still measure 2.67:1 — muted labels ('Operations', 'Unassigned', '—', the breadcrumb slash), all of them --n400 at 70% lightness on white. Retuning the primary theme's neutral ramp changes every screen in the product and wants a designer's eye across all of them; it is a design decision, not a bug fix, so it is named here rather than made quietly.

tests.title: The app at phone width
tests.intro: The field role is the one most likely to be on a phone, and the one nobody has tested on one.
steps: Emulate a 375×812 viewport.
Open Dashboard, Work Orders, a work order and Scan.
Check the nav is reachable and nothing overflows the screen horizontally.
tests.expect: Content fits the width, the sidebar collapses to something reachable, and no page scrolls sideways.
tests.notes: Emulated 375×812 as the Field Technician. Dashboard, Work Orders, a work-order detail and /scan all report documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth === 375, so nothing scrolls the page sideways; the KPI tiles stack two-up, and Recent Work Orders scrolls inside its own box (321 visible of 662) which is the correct behaviour rather than a defect. The sidebar collapses behind a hamburger which opens a 220px drawer carrying the whole nav, and the work-order detail opens full width without overflow. Only clipping seen is text ellipsis on the org name and the breadcrumb. HONESTY NOTE: with the pane hidden, pointer clicks in the emulated mobile viewport timed out, so the drawer and the work-order detail were opened with element.click() rather than real pointer input. The layout measurements are read from the rendered DOM and are unaffected; the hit-testing of those two controls at phone width is not proved.

tests.title: Keyboard only: reach and use the primary action
tests.intro: Tab order and visible focus, on the busiest list in the app.
steps: On Assets, tab from the top of the page.
Watch for a visible focus ring at each stop.
Reach the primary button and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>.
tests.expect: Focus is visible at every stop, order follows the page, and the button fires from the keyboard.
tests.notes: Half observed, half unprovable. OBSERVED GOOD: tabbing through Assets moves focus in DOM order — type select, location select, then each row's View / Edit / WO in turn — and every one of the 15 stops recorded carries a visible focus ring (outline: auto 1px, the UA default; the app defines no focus-visible style of its own). Shift+Tab from the search box lands on 'Add Asset', so the primary action is reachable. NOT PROVABLE: pressing Return and then space on that focused button did nothing — no modal, no request. That is the same limitation round 2 recorded for F3: this pane's synthetic key events move focus and type text but do not appear to produce a browser's default key-to-activation behaviour, and round 2 showed the same silence on the simplest form in the app. So neither a pass nor a fail can be claimed for activation, and it is left unrun rather than guessed. Thirty seconds from a human with a real keyboard settles it.

tests.title: Double-submit a create form
tests.intro: The classic duplicate: an impatient second click before the first request answers.
steps: Open a create form (a risk or a work order).
Fill it and click Save twice in quick succession.
Check the list.
tests.expect: One record, not two — the button disables or the second submit is swallowed.
tests.notes: Filled New WO with the title 'UAT R3 — double submit probe' and clicked 'Create work order' twice back to back. Exactly one record: WO-2026-0003, and the list went from 7 rows to 8. The guard is real rather than lucky — the submit button is `disabled={saving}` and relabels to 'Creating…' while the request is in flight (WorkOrders.jsx:150-151). CAVEAT ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS: the two clicks were separate tool calls, so they were a few hundred milliseconds apart rather than a true human double-click; the disabled attribute is what makes me confident, not the timing.

tests.title: Search, filter and sort agree with each other
tests.intro: Three controls over one list is where counts and rows stop matching.
steps: On Assets, search for a term matching one asset.
Apply a status filter alongside it.
Sort by a column and check the row count and any 'showing N' figure still agree.
tests.expect: The rows shown match the filters, and every count on the page agrees with the rows.
tests.notes: On Assets, searching 'Warri' left exactly 2 rows (NGML-VLV-0089, NGML-SCR-041) and the header read '2 assets'. Adding the Standby state filter on top left exactly 1 row (NGML-SCR-041, the only Standby asset) and the header read '1 asset', pluralised correctly. Counts and rows agree in every combination tried. Two things the card asked for that are not there: the table has no sort — the column headers are plain <th> with no handler — so the sort clause could not be exercised; and the header sentence mixes scopes, reading '1 asset · 4 locations · 5 sites' where the asset count is filtered and the location and site counts are not.

tests.title: Back button after sign-out
tests.intro: The cheapest data leak there is: a cached page rendering after the session is gone.
steps: Sign in, open Assets, sign out.
Press the browser Back button.
Read what renders.
tests.expect: The sign-in screen, or a redirect to it. No asset data behind a dead session.
tests.notes: Signed in as the owner, opened /assets, signed out through the account menu (landed on /auth), then pressed the browser Back button. The sign-in form is what came back: location is /auth, the page contains no asset data (searched for NGML-MTR-0042 — absent), and the form is the live one, not a cached render.

tests.title: CSV import: the template and the picker
tests.intro: r1t50. The import modal takes a file through a native picker, which this session cannot open. The template download in the same modal can be checked, and its headers are what an importer has to match.
steps: Assets → Import CSV.
Download the template.
Check its header row against what the importer expects.
tests.expect: The template downloads and its headers are the ones the parser reads.
tests.notes:
The template the button hands you is broken. Pressing 'Download template' does fire a real download named asset-import-template.csv (the blob was captured at creation to read what it contains, since the pane's sandbox blocks the save). Its header row has 18 columns — ain,name,category,location,site,status,manufacturer,model,serial_number,install_date,purchase_date,runtime_hours,value,last_maintenance_date,next_maintenance_date,tags,lat,lng — and those are the right ones; parseCSV maps values to whatever headers it finds. But the example row underneath has NINETEEN values: an extra '90' sits after value and before the dates. From column 14 on, every value is one place left of its header: last_maintenance_date gets '90', next_maintenance_date gets 2025-06-01, tags gets a date, lat gets 'critical,offshore', lng gets 6.45, and 3.4 falls off the end. Cause is visible at Assets.jsx:228 — the comment above CSV_HEADERS says health_score was deliberately removed from the header list because it is derived, and the example array was never trimmed to match. Anyone who does the obvious thing — open the template, replace the sample row, import — imports garbage dates and coordinates. NOT RUN, and still not run: the import itself, which needs a native file picker this session cannot operate.

FIXED AND RE-RUN. The stray '90' is gone from the example row (Assets.jsx), and a length assertion now sits beside it so the next edit to CSV_HEADERS cannot silently desynchronise the two again. Re-captured the blob the button actually produces and parsed it: 18 headers, 18 values, aligned — last_maintenance_date=2025-06-01, next_maintenance_date=2025-12-01, tags=critical,offshore, lat=6.45, lng=3.4. Every pair now reads as its header says. STILL NOT RUN: the import itself, which needs a native file picker this session cannot operate. That half is unchanged and remains untested.

sections.title: Regressions on the round-2 fixes
sections.blurb: Four fixes from round 2 that a later change could plausibly undo, re-checked from the screen.

tests.title: The Viewer still cannot read the audit log
tests.intro: Round 2's F4: *:read no longer satisfies audit:read. The Viewer reaching the Admin audit tab was the symptom.
steps: Sign in as the Viewer.
Type /admin into the address bar directly — do not just check the nav.
Look for an audit or activity log tab.
tests.expect: No audit log. Bounced to the dashboard, or the tab is absent.
tests.notes: Signed in as uat.viewer and typed /admin into the address bar rather than trusting the nav. Redirected to /dashboard; the sidebar carries no Admin entry and the page contains no audit or activity log. Round 2's EXPLICIT_ONLY_CAPS carve-out still holds.

tests.title: Depreciation preview still computes
tests.intro: Round 2's F10: a non-existent commission_date column made every basis lookup 500.
steps: Depreciation → preview a schedule on an asset.
Read the first year's charge.
tests.expect: A schedule preview with figures, not internal_error.
tests.notes: Depreciation → New Schedule → NGML-MTR-0042. The asset has no useful life, and the app says so in a sentence — 'This asset is missing part of its basis. Fill it in below, or add it on the asset record.' — rather than the internal_error round 1 saw. Supplying cost ₦240,000,000, salvage ₦24,000,000, life 20 years from 2020-09-07 rendered the full 20-row table with a charge of ₦10,800,000.00 a year, which is (240,000,000 − 24,000,000) ÷ 20 exactly, and closing balances stepping down row by row. The schedule was deliberately NOT created — the preview is what this card needed, and round 2 already left one fabricated schedule in the register.

tests.title: Health score still agrees with its own breakdown
tests.intro: Round 2's late find: the asset PATCH route ran a legacy decay engine, so any edit rewrote the score while the breakdown beneath it stayed on the five-signal engine.
steps: Open NGML-MTR-0042 and note the health score and its breakdown.
Edit the asset — change any field — and save.
Read the score and breakdown again.
tests.expect: The score is unchanged by an unrelated edit and still reconciles with the five signals listed beneath it.
tests.notes: NGML-MTR-0042 read 69, 'Calculated from 4 of 5 signals', with the working: Inspection condition 25/100 @25%, Open defects 80/100 @25%, Overdue maintenance 100/100 @20%, Risk level 80/100 @15%, Age against useful life excluded as no data. Edited the asset — set Manufacturer to 'UAT R3 Instruments', a field with no bearing on health — and saved ('Asset updated.'). The list still shows 69 and the reopened breakdown is unchanged and still reconciles: (25×.25 + 80×.25 + 100×.20 + 80×.15) ÷ 0.85 = 68.5 → 69. The legacy decay engine round 2 removed from the PATCH path has stayed removed.

tests.title: No raw error codes anywhere the run touched
tests.intro: Round 2 replaced the displayed error at 113 call sites across 25 files. This is a standing check across every refusal this round provokes rather than a separate click-through.
steps: Across every refusal triggered in this round, read the text on screen.
Watch the console for anything thrown behind a clean-looking page.
tests.expect: Every refusal reads as a sentence. No snake_case code shown to a user.
tests.notes:
No snake_case code reached a screen anywhere in this round — that half of round 2's sweep holds. Every refusal provoked read as English: 'There is not enough on hand for that issue.', 'No asset with tag “NGML-NOPE-9999” in this organisation.', 'This asset is missing part of its basis…', 'This job has no cost on it yet, so it will be sent as ₦0…'. Two failures against the rest of the expectation, both recorded on their own cards. One refusal produced NO message at all: the Viewer's POST /api/reports is refused 403 and the screen says nothing, because the error is written to a variable only rendered on a different tab. One misdescribes itself: an inverted approval band is a client mistake the API is written to answer 422 invalid_band, but the PATCH path escapes as a 500 and the user is told 'Something went wrong at our end… tell an administrator'. A silent refusal is worse for the user than the code would have been. Console across the whole run: only React Router v7 future-flag warnings plus the 403s this round deliberately provoked — nothing thrown.

FIXED AND RE-RUN. Both failures are closed. The Viewer's silent refusal is gone — the create control is no longer offered to a role that cannot use it, and the message is rendered on the generate tab as well as the library. The approval band no longer misdescribes itself: it answers 422 and reads 'The ceiling has to be above the floor.' instead of 'Something went wrong at our end.' A third refusal was improved while here: closing a job against missing stock now reads 'Not enough stock to close this job: SP-PT-1100 — need 12, 1 on hand.' — watched on screen — where it previously discarded the shortfall detail the API had already returned. No snake_case code appeared anywhere in either the run or the re-run.
